gen-dafont-ozone-gf-noto-serif-ahom: Ozone draws stems and crossbars at a single thickness, with wide-set curve ends that give its round letters a technical look. Noto Serif Ahom, lofty and dignified, tapers its joins gently, so give it a little extra size.
gen-dafont-ozone-gf-noto-serif-armenian: Technical and geometric, Ozone keeps every line plain and unmodulated. Noto Serif Armenian adds a faint swell to each curve, like pulled taffy, and Ozone looks best blown up for a word or two.
gen-dafont-ozone-gf-noto-serif-balinese: Editorial lowercase with real vertical presence carries the text, with Ozone keeping its own lines flat and uniform. Noto Serif Balinese settles between flat and dramatic strokes, while Ozone, with no up-versus-side difference, suits large display lines.
gen-dafont-ozone-gf-noto-serif-bengali: Ozone looks drawn with a compass pencil, consistent from stem to curve. Noto Serif Bengali, with fine hairlines and curves that thin modestly as they turn, would settle into a dense, refined texture down a full column.
gen-dafont-ozone-gf-noto-serif-devanagar: Ozone bends its strokes like a paperclip, geometric and technical. Noto Serif Devanagari keeps stems and connecting strokes only slightly apart in weight, and its short ascenders over large lowercase forms let paragraphs glide along.
gen-dafont-ozone-gf-noto-serif-ethiopic: Crisp and mechanical: Ozone draws its g in one unchanging line weight, with wide-set curve ends. And Noto Serif Ethiopic lets words settle into solid blocks, its diagonals a touch lighter than its verticals.
gen-dafont-ozone-gf-noto-serif-gurmukhi: Noto Serif Gurmukhi has a generous x-height, plus a soft, gradual thickening like a lightly pressed brush. Noto Serif Gurmukhi rewards a slightly larger size, while Ozone stays monoline from stem to serif.
gen-dafont-ozone-gf-noto-serif-hebrew: Technical and wiry, Ozone looks cut from bent wire. Noto Serif Hebrew adds a sturdy, tall-bodied lowercase with gentle modulation, so the wire-like heading and the softer text sit comfortably together on the page.
gen-dafont-ozone-gf-noto-serif-khojki: Flat, drafted and geometric: Ozone gives every glyph a single line weight, with wide-set curve ends. Noto Serif Khojki, refined and literary, puts short ascenders above big bowls, and its moderate contrast keeps paragraphs moving smoothly.
gen-dafont-ozone-gf-noto-serif-sinhala: Noto Serif Sinhala is refined and bookish, with short stalks above a lofty band of letters, its weights differing just enough. Ozone stays rigid; paragraphs below flow with a lively texture.
